files.SKILL.md:
---
name: code-review
description: Review a diff or pull request for bugs, risks and missing tests
---

# Code review
1. Run `git diff` (or `git diff main...HEAD`) and read every changed file in full context.
2. Look for: logic errors, unhandled edge cases, security issues, race conditions, API breakage, missing tests.
3. Report findings ordered by severity, each with file:line, why it is a problem and a concrete fix.
4. Do not comment on style unless it hides a bug. If nothing is wrong, say so plainly.

items.title: git-commit
items.desc: Write clear Conventional Commit messages from staged changes

files.SKILL.md:
---
name: git-commit
description: Write clear Conventional Commit messages from staged changes
---

# Git commit
1. Run `git status` and `git diff --staged`. If nothing is staged, ask what to stage.
2. Write a subject line `type(scope): summary` (feat, fix, refactor, docs, test, chore), max 72 chars, imperative mood.
3. Add a short body explaining *why* when the change is not obvious.
4. Commit with `git commit`. Never push unless asked.

items.desc_ru: Системная отладка: воспроизвести, изолировать, исправить, проверить

files.SKILL.md:
---
name: debugging
description: Systematic root-cause debugging: reproduce, isolate, fix, verify
---

# Debugging
1. Reproduce the failure first and capture the exact error. No fix before a reproduction.
2. Form 2-3 hypotheses, test the cheapest first (logs, minimal repro, bisect with `git bisect`).
3. Fix the root cause, not the symptom. Keep the change minimal.
4. Add a regression test, rerun the original reproduction and the test suite.

items.title: write-tests
items.desc: Add focused unit tests that match the project conventions

files.SKILL.md:
---
name: write-tests
description: Add focused unit tests that match the project conventions
---

# Writing tests
1. Find the existing test framework and naming conventions before writing anything.
2. Cover the happy path, boundaries, error paths and one regression case per bug.
3. Prefer small deterministic tests; avoid network, time and randomness unless injected.
4. Run the tests and show the result. Fix flaky tests instead of retrying them.

items.title: refactor-safely
items.desc: Refactor in small verified steps without changing behavior

files.SKILL.md:
---
name: refactor-safely
description: Refactor in small verified steps without changing behavior
---

# Safe refactoring
1. Make sure tests pass before you start; add characterization tests if coverage is missing.
2. One kind of change per step (rename, extract, move). Run the tests after each step.
3. Never mix refactoring with behavior changes in the same commit.
4. Summarize what moved and confirm that behavior is unchanged.

name: explain-codebase
description: Map an unfamiliar repository: entry points, structure, data flow
---

# Explain a codebase
1. Read README, build files and the top-level tree. Use `rg --files` and `rg` to find entry points.
2. Describe: purpose, main modules, how data flows, how to build, run and test.
3. Point to specific files with `path:line`. Flag dead code, risky areas and missing docs.
4. End with a short "where to start changing X" guide.

name: android-dev
description: Build, test and lint Android projects from the command line
---

# Android development
1. Use the Gradle wrapper: `./gradlew assembleDebug`, `testDebugUnitTest`, `lint`.
2. Read build errors from the first failure up; fix root causes in Manifest, resources and Gradle files.
3. Keep minSdk/targetSdk decisions explicit and mention permission or lifecycle impacts of a change.
4. Prefer small, testable classes; keep UI work on the main thread and I/O off it.

files.SKILL.md:
---
name: security-audit
description: Look for common vulnerabilities and leaked secrets in a repository
---

# Security audit
1. Search for secrets: `rg -n "(api[_-]?key|secret|token|password)\s*[:=]"` and review `.env` files and history.
2. Check input handling (injection, path traversal, deserialization), authN/authZ and dependency risks.
3. Rate each finding (critical/high/medium/low) with an exploit scenario and a fix.
4. Do not exploit anything; report only.
